title: k8s-helm-node-provisioning-debug-scratchpad
summary: Working notes for debugging node provisioning failures during cluster scale-up; commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.
content:
Context:
- Small cluster (3 control-plane, 8 workers) on AWS EC2 (autoscaling group + launch template). Using kubeadm provisioning + kubelet systemd service + cluster-autoscaler via Helm.
- Issue: intermittent node provisioning failures during autoscaler spin up. Nodes reach EC2 running but never become Ready or kubelet keeps restarting. Seen across multiple AZs.

Timeline / symptoms:
- Autoscaler launches instance -> instance boots -> cloud-init runs -> kubelet service starts -> instance sometimes stays NotReady and kubelet logs show repeated TLS/bootstrap errors or volume attach timeouts.
- Sometimes node registers and then immediately Gets KubeletImagePullBackOff for pause container (we use custom pause image) or kube-proxy fails due to failing iptables setup.

Commands I ran (raw):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  OUTPUT: 
  NAME                STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP     EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION
  ip-10-0-3-45.ec2... NotReady    <none>   5m    v1.27.3   10.0.3.45       52.0.12.34    Ubuntu 22.04 LTS       5.15.0-1019-aws

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-3-45.ec2.internal
  Key parts: 
  Events:
    2m   Normal  Starting                 kubelet
    1m   Warning FailedMount            Unable to attach or mount volumes: timed out waiting for the condition
    30s  Warning  NodeNotReady            Kubelet stopped posting node status.

- ssh ubuntu@10.0.3.45 
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | tail -n 200
  Snippets: 
  "E0302 12:14:09.123456    1234 kubelet.go:2345] Node not registered: timed out waiting for the condition"
  "W0302 12:14:10.234567    1234 kubelet_server.go:456] Failed to update kubelet config: getting bootstrap tokens: file not found: /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubeconfig"
  "E0302 12:14:15.345678    1234 docker_container.go:789] Failed to pull image \"k8s.gcr.io/pause:3.8\": unauthorized: authentication required"

- sudo systemctl status kubelet
  Output: Active: active (running) but RestartCount: 4 (restart loop)

- ls -l /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubeconfig
  -> file missing on some nodes (observed); present on others.

- cat /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf
  -> environment contains KUBELET_KUBEADM_ARGS=--bootstrap-kubeconfig=/var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubeconfig --kubeconfig=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf

- sudo journalctl -u cloud-init -b | grep kubeadm -n
  Found cloud-init script running kubeadm join but exiting with non-zero on some runs: "join command failed: exit status 2"

- sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
  Snippet: "[ERROR] kubeadm join --token XXXXX --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:YYYYY failed: could not access bootstrap config: permission denied"

- aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0abc12345 --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].StateTransitionReason'
  -> shows normal boot, not stopped/terminated by ASG.

- kubectl logs -n kube-system deployment/cluster-autoscaler --since=1h
  Snippet: "scale-up: launching 1 node(s) in cluster (group: asg-workers-us-east-1a)" then "node didn't become ready: timeout"

- helm list -n kube-system
  -> cluster-autoscaler chart v1.21.0 (custom values)

- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep kube-proxy
  Some nodes show kube-proxy CrashLoopBackOff with error: "iptables: Chain 'KUBE-SERVICES' does not exist."

Hypotheses so far:
1) bootstrap-kubeconfig missing or permissions problem from cloud-init race (kubeadm join not creating files or cloud-init finishing before certain steps).
   - Evidence: bootstrap file missing on NotReady nodes, cloud-init logs show permission denied errors.
   - Possible causes: cloud-init user-data script is running as non-root or does sudo but the file creation path uses different UID/GID; or ephemeral disk mount timing (e.g., /var is on a separate volume mounted later).

2) Network/CNI timing issues causing kube-proxy/iptables setup to fail, resulting in pods not starting and kubelet marking NotReady (or reporting network plugin not ready).
   - Evidence: kube-proxy CrashLoopBackOff, iptables missing chains.
   - Possible cause: CNI plugin (weave/Calico) daemonset failing because kubelet lacks proper cgroups or CRI not fully started.

3) Image pull/auth problems for pause image (private registry creds missing on new node).
   - Evidence: unauthorized errors pulling pause container on some nodes.
   - Possible cause: in our setup we mirror pause image to our private ECR; new node's IAM role might not have ECR permissions in the AZ or instance profile is not attached correctly in the launch template.

4) Volume attach/mount timeouts: EBS volumes (used for kubelet local storage or CSI) sometimes stuck attaching and cause pod failures and kubelet errors.
   - Evidence: FailedMount events and aws attach volume logs show timeout after multiple retries.

Commands tried to reproduce/mitigate interactively:
- Forced a new node: edited ASG desired capacity + waited
- On a failing node: sudo touch /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubeconfig && sudo chown root:root /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubeconfig && systemctl restart kubelet
  Result: in one case node progressed to Ready after kubeadm re-ran and created /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf. Suggests missing file was bottleneck.

- For image pull issue: aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <account>.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com then docker pull <pause-image> worked from node when run manually; suggests instance role vs manual credentials difference.

- Temporarily disabled IMDSv2 enforcement in launch template (to test token issues) and tried new instance; no regression reproduced yet.

- Increased kubelet systemd service start delay by adding ExecStartPre sleep 10 (temporary) to see race; mixed results (one node worked, another still failed).

- Re-applied Helm chart for cluster-autoscaler with higher scaleUpDelay and backoff settings to reduce churn.

Notes about config and where to look next:
- cloud-init user-data (launch template) script: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/launch-templates#cloud-init (linked_artifact) -> verify order, check for "set -e" and sudo uses.
- kubeadm/kubelet config: /etc/kubernetes/manifests vs /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf generation step. Search cloud-init logs for kubeadm commands.
- IAM role for instance profile: check that new nodes assume correct profile and have ecr:GetAuthorizationToken + ecr:BatchGetImage + ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer permissions. Also ensure instance profile attached to ASG launches (not per-instance override).
- Check whether /var is a separate volume (launch template uses ephemeral/ebs) so mount race possible.
- Check kube-proxy and CNI daemonset logs: kubectl logs -n kube-system daemonset/calico-node or weave-net for failures.

Quick checklist for next reproduction steps:
- 1) Spin up a new node in staging ASG with modified user-data that prints environment + id-token status, and write debug files at each step.
- 2) Add sleeps between cloud-init kubeadm join and file operations to test race.
- 3) Validate instance profile IAM permissions by adding a debug step to call aws sts get-caller-identity and aws ecr get-login-password in cloud-init and log output.
- 4) Run kubeadm token create --ttl 24h on control plane and pin token in test user-data to avoid discovery token expiry.
- 5) Verify network policies and kube-proxy iptables: capture iptables-save output in cloud-init pre-start script for later inspection.

Links / artifacts / tickets:
- INF-1123 (Jira): autoscaler failing to provision nodes intermittently
- slack thread: #infra-incident (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345)
- internal repo: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/launch-templates (cloud-init user-data)
- helm values for cluster-autoscaler: git PR https://git.redwood/internal/infra/helm-charts/pull/45

Immediate actions I took (summary):
- Added temporary guard (touch bootstrap-kubeconfig + chown) via cloud-init user-data in a staging LT and reproduced success once.
- Added more logging to cloud-init and increased kubelet start delay in staging to gather more data.
- Opened INF-1123 and assigned to eng-platform-engineering (cc: Priya, Jordan).

Observations to capture later:
- If bootstrap file creation is inconsistent, we should consider moving kubeadm join into a systemd unit with proper After= mounts and network-online.target to avoid cloud-init race.
- If ECR auth fails intermittently, we may need to attach an instance role that pre-populates /etc/docker/config.json via cloud-init using instance-role credentials rather than relying on instance metadata.

Next-steps (concrete):
- Reproduce in staging with debug user-data and collect full journalctl, cloud-init logs, and aws ec2 describe-volume-attachments for failed node.
- If reproduced, convert cloud-init kubeadm join into systemd unit with explicit ordering and retry logic.
- Validate IAM role on a fresh launch and check ECR permissions.
- Consider swapping pause image to public registry for testing to rule out ECR issues.

Random notes / TODO:
- Check KubeletVersion mismatch? control-plane v1.27.3, new nodes use same AMI but verify AMI pipeline.
- Investigate kubelet service file differences between working and failing AMIs (maybe older cloud-init baked image).
- Run a curl to metadata service to validate IMDSv2 token requirement in cloud-init flows.

--- end of scratchpad (will update as I get more logs)
